I'm writing this article just as I'm about to set off on a short trip up north. Every time I leave home, there are a few essential devices in my smart home system that I rely on completely to keep everything running smoothly. A quick reminder: to control your devices remotely and access all the features below, you'll need a dedicated Apple Home hub, such as an Apple TV 4K or HomePod.

The "HomeKit Weekly" series covers smart home accessories, automation tips and tricks, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

Outdoor watering system automation

Where I live, the weather gets unbearably hot. You can bet that whenever you're not home, you're praying for rain — otherwise you'll have to do the watering yourself. If you're travelling in summer, automatic watering is hands down one of the simplest and most practical smart home applications. If you've ever come back from a week away to find a patch of lawn or a few potted plants completely dead, you'll know exactly what I mean. There are plenty of smart products on the market that connect directly to your tap, letting you manually turn on sprinklers or set up automations based on specific times and local weather conditions.

Walk into a comfortable indoor temperature the moment you get home

Coming home from a long trip to a hot, stuffy house where the air conditioning takes forever to cool down — that's the worst feeling. On the other hand, though, leaving the air conditioning running for ages just to maintain a set temperature in an empty house is a real waste. If you use a smart thermostat that supports Apple Home, you can remotely adjust the air conditioning to your preferred temperature the night before. I've been using this method for several years now. I like to run the air conditioning overnight, letting the unit bring the temperature back down during the coolest part of the day. That saves money and also reduces unnecessary wear on the air conditioner.

Automate lights on and off to create the illusion that someone's home

One of the most traditional ways to deter burglars is to leave a few lights on so the house looks occupied. The problem is, if the same lamp stays on day and night, you're basically telling everyone on the street that nobody's home. This is where Apple Home really comes into its own. Set up automations for a few main lights, and you can control them manually from anywhere, or set random schedules to truly create the impression that someone is moving around the house.

Monitor your home with HomeKit cameras

When I'm on a trip, I certainly don't want to be worrying about home all the time, but I do want to know if anything's happening. In fact, last year while I was travelling, a single notification helped me spot a small problem straight away. That's why I trust HomeKit Secure Video. I've set up a few cameras around the outside of the house to keep an eye on the surroundings. With HomeKit Secure Video, all recordings are stored securely in iCloud+, and since I use two Apple TVs as hubs, I can view live footage and recorded clips from anywhere, anytime, as long as I have an internet connection.

Wrapping up

Summer is a great time to travel, but extreme heat also means you need to keep a closer eye on things at home. With the right Apple Home setup, you can keep your lawn watered, walk into a refreshingly cool house, have lights switching on and off at random intervals, and check live camera feeds from anywhere. These are exactly the setups I use when I'm travelling for work or when the whole family goes on a trip — they really do make the whole journey much easier.
